ambiguities.text: BLOCK_HASH_OR_HEIGHT is not clearly defined - unclear if both formats must be supported or just one
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume compliant explorers SHOULD support both block hashes (0x-prefixed hex) and block heights (decimal integers) for the /block/ endpoint.

ambiguities.text: No specification for error handling when the requested resource (block, tx, address, token) does not exist
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume explorers should return appropriate HTTP 404 responses with user-friendly error pages for non-existent resources.

ambiguities.text: The distinction between 'address' and 'token' endpoints is vague - tokens are also addresses
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume /address/ is for EOAs and all contracts, while /token/ is specifically for ERC-20/ERC-721 token contract views with token-specific information.

implicit_assumptions.description: Block explorers are trusted to display accurate blockchain data matching the provided identifiers
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Malicious explorers could display fabricated transaction or block data, leading users to believe false information about blockchain state.

implicit_assumptions.description: The blockchain data source used by the explorer is synchronized and accurate
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Stale or incorrect data could be displayed, misleading users about transaction confirmations or account balances.

implicit_assumptions.description: Attackers cannot inject malicious content through URL path parameters
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: URL path injection could lead to XSS attacks, path traversal, or other web vulnerabilities in the block explorer.
